MEASURED in a throwaway repo (de, 2026-09-04): the filter is only HALF the mechanism and either half alone loses the failure. (1) The error text carries neither REFUS nor FAIL -- 'error: pathspec

did not match any file(s) known to git' -- so grep -ciE 'refus|fail' over it returns 0 and a wider pattern would not have caught it. (2) THE PIPE REPLACES THE EXIT CODE: 'git commit 2>&1 | head -3' exits 0 while the same command unpiped exits 1, so even an unfiltered grep shows a green shell. (3) Nothing is staged and nothing is committed -- the failure is total, not partial. So the durable fix is shape, not vocabulary: a write runs unfiltered and its exit status is read (or set -o pipefail), because a filter over a write's output cannot tell 'nothing needed doing' from 'it failed' and a pipe additionally discards the one signal that could. 'git add && git commit' is immune: add creates the index entry, so commit sees a tracked path.
